title: Completion-unit tensor insertions and coherent pullback tensor comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ and the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$ and $u_c^*=C_{\mathcal X}u^*\dashv P$ on complete objects. For arbitrary $V,W\in D_T$ the maps
$$C_T(\eta_{T,V}\otimes1_W):C_T(V\otimes_A^LW)\longrightarrow C_T(C_TV\otimes_A^LW),\qquad C_T(1_V\otimes\eta_{T,W})$$
are natural isomorphisms, as is
$$C_{\mathcal X}u^*(\eta_{\mathcal Y,V}):C_{\mathcal X}u^*V\longrightarrow C_{\mathcal X}u^*C_{\mathcal Y}V.$$
On complete objects put $V\widehat\otimes W=C_T(V\otimes_A^LW)$. There is a unique natural completed pullback tensor comparison
$$\mu^c_{V,W}:C_{\mathcal X}u^*C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes_A^LW)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\mathcal X}(C_{\mathcal X}u^*V\otimes_A^LC_{\mathcal X}u^*W)$$
whose composite with $C_{\mathcal X}u^*(\eta_{\mathcal Y,V\otimes W})$ equals $C_{\mathcal X}((\eta_{\mathcal X,u^*V}\otimes\eta_{\mathcal X,u^*W})\mu_{V,W})$, where $\mu$ is the ordinary pullback tensor comparison. These comparisons and the unit comparison induced from the ordinary tensor unit satisfy the associativity, symmetry and tensor-unit coherence equations. No perfectness of $A_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the unchanged tensor insertion and completed constraint interfaces, now reexported from the shared data module. For each complete Z, use the native tensorRight/RHom adjunction and internal-Hom completeness. Under these Hom bijections, precomposition by eta_X tensor 1 becomes precomposition by eta_X into a complete RHom. Reflection makes this bijective. Conjugate through reflection at the two tensor objects and test on source and target to construct the inverse of T(eta_X tensor 1).
Conjugate left insertion by the ordinary symmetric braiding to obtain right insertion. Apply the same argument on both sites. Compose left and right insertion to invert T(eta_X tensor eta_Y).

Use the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction and preservation of complete objects by direct image. Precomposition by L(eta_X), followed by reflection on the target, becomes the reflection bijection into the complete direct image. The same source-and-target Hom test gives invertibility of target-completed L(eta_X).

Apply the separate native pullback comparison lemma. It descends the actual complex-level left-derived counit to the homotopy category, uses the published native closed tensor models and the canonical derived comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives, and obtains the ordinary symmetric monoidal structure with exactly ConstantTensorNormalization. Its oplax unit laws give the required two ordinary action-unit equations.

Apply the tensor-compatible reflective-subcategory theorem on each site with the actual reflection bijections and insertion isomorphisms proved above. This gives the full complete subcategories their prescribed tensor objects, tensor maps, completed units and all four constraint formulas. Retain the same strong monoidal reflectors and their normalized comparison formulas for the completed functor factorization.

The same reflective-subcategory theorem supplies the pentagon, triangle, symmetric involution and hexagons for those formulas. These are separate categorical coherence checks; no extra perfectness assumption on the quotients is used.

Let a be the natural transformation target-completed L(eta) and b the ordinary comparison followed by target completion of the two target units. Naturality gives both transformations. All components of a and b are isomorphisms by steps 2 and 3. Define mu_c as a inverse followed by b. Cancel a to prove both normalization and uniqueness. Define e_c similarly from a at the ordinary unit and target completion of e.

Apply the normalized completed-pullback coherence theorem to the two reflection data, ordinary symmetric monoidal comparison, the normalized mu_c and e_c, and both exact completed constraint models. It supplies oplax monoidal coherence for completeInverse. Supply the strong reflector structures and formulas retained in step 5; all parts of this categorical coherence theorem are proved in this packet.

The same coherence theorem identifies the cotensorator and unit with the separately constructed normalized comparisons and supplies the completed symmetry square. Combine these with all insertion isomorphisms, ordinary unit laws, normalization and uniqueness.
